issue.title: Accept dates with two-digit years (31/10/26)
issue.body:
Our corporate card provider writes dates as `31/10/26`, with a two-digit year.
Every file fails at the first transaction with 'The date could not be read'.
The same file with `31/10/2026` imports fine. Could two-digit years be read as
20xx? The provider says it can't change the format.

input.title: Accept two-digit years in day-first statement dates
input.body:
File: src/util/dates.ts

The DAY_FIRST pattern in parseStatementDate only matches a four-digit year (\d{4}), so 31/10/26 is rejected with errors.badDate. Extend the pattern to accept a two-digit year and map it to 20xx (for example 2000 + yy), keeping the existing calendar validation afterwards. Four-digit years must keep working as before.
